To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the physics of constraints is a necessary basis for the physics of symbols and for bridging the genotype-phenotypic epistemic cut in biological evolution; (b) the physics of symbols is a necessary basis to bridge the epistemic cuts of all higher-level phenomena, from the origin of life and biological evolution to the origin of language, culture and consciousness; (c) the physics of non-integrable constraints, which are necessary for bridging epistemic cuts and
the physics of symbols is the physics of the genotype-phenote distinction, which is the physics of evolution.
The physics of symbols bridges the epistemic gap between genotype and phenotype by measurement and coding.

how non-integrable constraints bridge the epistemic gap between the genotype and the phenotype.

the physics of symbols is a necessary condition for biological evolution.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
evolution is the process of constructing and using symbols to measure and control the dynamics of construction.
evolution requires non-integrable constraints that are also heterogeneous in their constraints and in their dynamics.
evolution is a process of self-organization that requires the genotype- phenotype distinction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the physics of symbols is a fundamental problem for biology, and that this physics is a natural extension of the physics of measurement and control that underpins all technology.
the physics of constraints is essential to the understanding of the origin of life, and that the physics of information, as it is usually formulated, cannot explain life's origin.
the genotype-phenote distinction is a necessary condition for evolution and is a universal property of all complex systems that evolve by natural selection.
